MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 27, 2021
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:02 p.m., on April 27, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on April 23, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:10 p.m.)
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  Council Member Goodell

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Stein Mart Property 25282 Marguerite
  Parkway; Agency Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, Keith Rattay, Elaine Lister, Cheryl
  Dyas and William Curley. Negotiating Party: Kinstler Family Trust. Under Negotiation-
  Price and Terms

CS2. Liability Claims and Existing Litigation: Claimants: Driscoll, Cunningham, Roth,
  Nshanian, DeMott, Maul: Agency Claimed Against-City of Mission Viejo and:
  Significant Exposure to Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9 (6 cases).

CS3. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Significant Exposure to
  Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) or (3) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1
  case).
City Council Minutes  1  April 27, 2021
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with four Council Members present (Council Member Goodell was
absent).

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were three Closed Session Items this evening. The
City Council was updated and gave staff direction, but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Featured Business of the Month – Oggi’s Pizza

  Presented proclamation to Business Owner Kanwal Mundy.

P2. School Spotlight - Viejo Elementary School

  Received presentation from Principal Jesus Becerra.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Mark Neely, M.V.: Spoke about racism in the Country and asked about humanity within the
police force. Asked if he can meet with the police department to share his concerns.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Spoke about Community Choice Energy and asked that the City look into
joining the Orange County Power Authority.

Written comments were submitted by Michelle Schumacher and Denise Colber with concerns
over the Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) debt and the impact on taxpayers.

Written comment was submitted by Stephen Wontrobski regarding water quality at 27132
Sombras that is supplied by Santa Margarita Water District.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
City Council Minutes  2  April 27, 2021
 ABSENT:  Goodell

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of April 13, 2021, presented.

2.  Check Register Dated April 9, 2021 in the Amount of $3,986,520.55

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Contract Amendment for Janitorial and Related Services for All City Facilities and
  Recreation

  Approved fourth amendment for Alliance Building Maintenance for janitorial related
  services for all city facilities and recreation centers for the period of July 1, 2020 to June 30,
  2021 in an amount not to exceed $160,000.00

4.  Resurfacing of Tennis Courts at the Felipe Tennis Center

  Awarded a contract for the resurfacing of the six (6) tennis courts at the Felipe Tennis
  Center to Taylor Tennis Courts in an amount not to exceed $42,451.00.

5.  Rubberized Surfacing Replacement - Florence Joyner Olympiad Park

  (1) Awarded a contract to T.J. Janca Construction, Inc. for the Rubberized Surfacing
  Replacement - Florence Joyner Olympiad Park in an amount not to exceed $78,002.77, and
  (2) issued a purchase order to T.J. Janca Construction, Inc. for an amount not to exceed
  $78,002.77 .

6.  2021 Residential Resurfacing - Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 22838)

  Approved the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer,
  and authorize staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

7.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

8.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.
City Council Minutes  3  April 27, 2021
 Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths commented on the beautiful landscaping throughout the City. He pointed
out that when the El Toro Marine Corp left and went down to Miramar they took the Flying
Leatherneck Aviation Museum which is now closed due to budget constraints. He has been talking
with the Irvine City Council and there is a good chance it will come back to the Great Park.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs said it was great to be back in the Chamber. He stated he has had it with
the mask issues, and questioned why people are wearing masks while driving in their cars and stated
he will not be wearing a mask outdoors. He outlined several reasons that it’s not healthy to wear a
mask outside. He commented that he was conflicted about the public speaker this evening and
expressed his opinion on recent events regarding police shootings. Lastly, he stated that he had
breakfast this morning at the Terrace on the Green at the Oso Creek Golf Course and said the food
and wait staff was fantastic.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum thanked Chief of Police by getting up and welcoming the public speaker
this evening. She shared that she attended the Mission Viejo Girls Softball end of season parade
and had a wonderful time. She also stopped by Food Drive that benefited the Family Assistance
Ministries last week and gave kudos to staff. Announced that the Norman P. Community Center
will reopen on May 3. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum stated that she was re-installed as a board member
to the Association of California Cities-Orange County. She shared that there is a study from
Stanford regarding mask wearing and attended an event on human trafficking that talked about the
usage of masks on children. Lastly, she is very happy to be back in the Council Chamber and stated
that she tried to oppose a bill that was introduced by Senator Pat Bates that impedes the financing
of the 241 Toll Road.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley touched on the state legislation which is being sponsored and promoted by our Local
Senator Pat Bates. SB760 and SB761, SB760 was heard in the State Senate Transportation
Committee today. Mayor Kelley did listen in on the meeting and did speak in opposition.
Information will be coming out to our residents in the near future. SB760 would modify the
legislative description for the termini of state route 241. Current law establishes the State Highway
System throughout California and designates SR241, the I-5 South of the City of San Clemente to
State Route 91 in Anaheim. She stated that this Bill would delete from the State Highway System
the portion of SR241 South of San Clemente to Oso Parkway, it’s identical to SB1373 which
Senator Bates sponsored last year which our City also opposed. This would terminate the SR241
at Oso Parkway into perpetuity which can have adverse effects on local jurisdictions by distributing
regional traffic on our local arterial roads. Mayor Kelley indicated that the City has met with
Senator Bates and asked her not to pursue this legislation. We don’t need Sacramento making local
transportation decisions, they are already very involved in our local decisions and we have lost a
lot of local control to Sacramento and we need to have local control over our transportation
decisions. She pointed out that there are mechanisms at the local level to identify options and to
develop solutions. These Bills exempt San Clemente from regional transportation planning at the
City Council Minutes  4  April 27, 2021
 expense of surrounding cities, and this could prohibit Orange County Transportation Authority
(OCTA), Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA), and Caltrans from looking at potential mobility
solutions in the future. These Bills are creating controversy between cities. The Bill was approved
by the Transportation Committee of the Senate but it still needs to be heard on the Senate floor and
then the Assembly. Mayor Kelley did attend the end of the season event for the Girls Mission Viejo
Softball. She commented on the mobile vaccination pod that was at Norman P. Murray Center last
Thursday and gave kudos to City Staff. Announced that the schools are back open. Lastly, she
thanked the Explorers for assisting visitors this evening.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:17 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Tuesday May 11, at 5:00 p.m.

Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 11, 2021

City Council Minutes  5  April 27, 2021
